about: A first-person narrator, a man, who speaks a woman's name in his own quoted words ('Mind the step, Lucy'); that name is a woman's, not the narrator's, and the narrator's gender shows only in how he is addressed ('sir').
title: The Night Ferry
author: Hollis Craymer

chapters.title: Crossing
paragraphs: I took the night ferry because it was the only boat that would carry a man with a horse and no papers.
The deckhand looked me over twice. "Straight down the ramp, sir, and mind the rope," he said at last.
I led the horse aboard and tied her at the rail. Lucy was already there, sitting on a crate with her bag on her knees.
"Mind the step, Lucy," I said, and held out my hand. She took it without a word.
We had not spoken since the harbour. I had told myself that silence was a kind of courtesy.
The engine shook the deck. Somewhere below us a pump began to knock, and the lamps swung on their hooks.
"Hang on to that crate, Lucy," I said when the first swell came, and she laughed for the first time that night.
The deckhand passed again with a lantern. "Rough water ahead, sir, you may want to go below," he told me.
I stayed on deck. I had spent too many years below deck on too many boats, and I wanted to see the far shore come.
Lucy fell asleep against my shoulder some time after midnight. I did not move for fear of waking her.
At dawn the coast showed grey and low on the water. I counted the lights of the town and found there were nine.
"Time to go ashore, sir," said the deckhand, and I woke Lucy and untied the horse.
